audit_findings.title: Legacy benefit obligations are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $225.863 million of total pension liabilities at 2025-12-31, including approximately $166.097 million of unfunded non-qualified obligations and approximately $60 million of multiemployer withdrawal liabilities; $211.398 million latest noncurrent pension and postretirement obligation at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: Recorded legacy obligations reduce the equity bridge unless their settlement cash flows are already fully deducted in OE; legally segregated qualified-plan assets cannot automatically offset unfunded non-qualified or withdrawal claims.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we sponsor several non-qualified pension plans, with unfunded obligations totaling approximately $166 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission from the stated bridge is demonstrated, although the proper net deduction still requires an OE-overlap reconciliation. The 2025 total equals about $1.36 per diluted share and 3.4% of base equity value, and is large relative to the $660.812 million cash bridge. It is therefore reasonably capable of changing valuation thresholds even though it would not reverse the conclusion that $67.28 exceeds every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 30 current and noncurrent pension and postretirement liabilities to benefit payments and charges already captured in OE, then rerun the bridge deducting only obligations not already reflected in OE and netting only legally available plan assets.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit long-term marketable securities after purging their income
audit_findings.magnitude: $555.497 million at 2026-06-30, equal to approximately $3.35 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Portfolio income was removed from OE, so the unrestricted investment principal must be added through the equity bridge; the stated $660.812 million equals June cash of $232.657 million plus short-term securities of $428.155 million and excludes long-term securities.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities of $1,167.9 million and approximately $400 million in available borrowings, and no amounts were outstanding under our credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possibility. Adding $555.497 million would increase base equity value by about 8.3% and value per share by about $3.35, which is reasonably capable of changing the valuation and margin-of-safety thresholds.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the long-term securities are unrestricted and non-operating, then rerun all scenarios with $555.497 million added to the June 30 bridge without restoring the purged portfolio income to OE.

audit_findings.title: The cash numerator and share denominator use different dates during an active repurchase program
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.7 million of July 2026 repurchases, approximately $0.11 per diluted share and 0.28% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation combines June 30 cash with a share denominator incorporating July 31 ownership, retaining cash that was spent to reduce the post-quarter share count.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, repurchases totaled approximately $165.3 million (excluding commissions and excise taxes), and we repurchased an additional $41.9 million (excluding commissions and excise taxes) between January 1, 2026 and February 18, 2026, fully utilizing the 2023 authorization, leaving approximately $308.2 million remaining under the 2025 authorization.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed July repurchase amount is only $18.7 million. Against $6.730 billion of base equity value and 165.819 million diluted shares, the maximum identified numerator overstatement is approximately 0.28% or $0.11 per share, too small to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: For date consistency, deduct the $18.7 million July repurchase expenditure from cash or rebuild the diluted share inventory as of June 30; also verify whether any other July transaction changes net equity rather than merely settling an already-recorded liability.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year OE anchor may rely on a capital-spending trough
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.016 million annual increase from $33.984 million of 2025 cash capital expenditures to $51 million expected for 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance portion above the 2025 deduction reduces sustainable anchor OE and all projected operating cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2026, we expect capital expenditures of approximately $51 million, which will be funded from cash on hand.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending forecast is filed, but the record does not establish how much is recurring maintenance rather than discretionary growth investment. If the entire $17.016 million increase were recurring maintenance, it would equal about 4.6% of the $366.1 million OE anchor, but the resulting valuation change cannot be established without classification and a rerun.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level support for headquarters, College Point and technology expenditures; classify maintenance, replacement and growth spending; normalize the OE anchor for the recurring maintenance amount and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $12.8 million residual in FY2017 and $9.1 million residual in FY2021, computed from the supplied filed-D&A coverage percentages
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual eligible D&A would increase historical OE and its trend, but the valuation anchors at the lower $366.1 million latest actual because the existing $373 million trend already exceeds it.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $49.1m (79.3% of filed D&A); FY2021 $48.4m (84.2% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value. Even adding the approximately $12.8 million and $9.1 million historical residuals would only raise the historical trend; under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule, that cannot lift the current $366.1 million anchor because the trend is already above it. The finding therefore has no present effect on scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset and amortization disclosures only if correcting the historical OE record is desired; rerun the valuation only if the classification would affect latest-year OE or another valuation input outside the capped historical trend.
